terminal.description: A shell in your workspace where try.js adds a workshop to data/kilnworth.db, restarts the API, then changes and removes it.

tasks.title: Add a workshop
tasks.description:
Implement `create(fields)` in `src/store.js`. `fields` is `{ title, day, seats, priceCents }`, already checked by the route. It adds a row to the `workshops` table, lets the database pick its `id`, and returns the new workshop as `{ id, title, day, seats, priceCents }`. Each value reaches the database in the place of a `?`.

The check posts two workshops to a database file of its own, restarts the server on the same file and lists the workshops again. It also reads the SQL your store hands the database.
nextSteps: Write an `INSERT` for the four fields, with a `?` for each.
Run it with the four values in the same order.
Read the id of the new row from the result of `run()`.
Return the new workshop and run `node try.js`.
hints: Leave `id` out of the `INSERT`: the `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` gives the row the next free number.
`run()` returns `{ changes, lastInsertRowid }`. `lastInsertRowid` is the id the new row got, and `get` reads a row by its id.

`const { lastInsertRowid } = db.prepare('INSERT INTO workshops (title, day, seats, priceCents) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)').run(fields.title, fields.day, fields.seats, fields.priceCents)`, then `return get(lastInsertRowid)`.

tasks.title: Change a workshop
tasks.description:
Implement `update(id, fields)` in `src/store.js`. `fields` holds some or all of `title`, `day`, `seats` and `priceCents`, already checked by the route.

- it changes only the columns in `fields`; the others keep what they hold
- it returns the whole workshop as it is now, or `undefined` when no row has that `id`
- it never adds a row

Each value, the id too, reaches the database in the place of a `?`. The check sends `PATCH` and `PUT` for ids in its table and for ids that are not, then looks at the table and at the SQL your store hands the database.
nextSteps: Write an `UPDATE` with a `WHERE` on the id.
Make a field that was not sent keep what the column holds.
Use the result of `run()` to tell whether a row was there.
Return the workshop as it is now, or `undefined`, and run `node try.js`.
hints: An `UPDATE` whose `WHERE` matches nothing is not an error. It runs and changes zero rows, and the result of `run()` says so.

`COALESCE(?, title)` keeps the title when the value is `NULL`. A field that was not sent is `undefined`, which SQLite cannot take, so hand over `fields.title ?? null`. `changes` is how many rows the statement changed.
`SET title = COALESCE(?, title), day = COALESCE(?, day), ...` with `WHERE id = ?`, then `.run(fields.title ?? null, ..., id)` and `return changes === 0 ? undefined : get(id)`.

videos.title: Update, delete and insert in SQL

tasks.title: Remove a workshop
tasks.description:
Implement `remove(id)` in `src/store.js`. It deletes the row whose `id` is `id` and returns `true`, or returns `false` when no row had that id. Only that row goes. The id reaches the database in the place of a `?`.

The check deletes a workshop twice, deletes an id that never had a row, then looks at what is left in the table and at the SQL your store hands the database.
nextSteps: Write a `DELETE` with a `WHERE` on the id.
Return whether it removed a row.
Run `node try.js` and look at the last answer.
hints: A `DELETE` that matches nothing runs without an error, so its result is the only way to know whether a row was there.
`changes` in the result of `run()` is the number of rows removed: 1 or 0 here.
